newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BCN sells stake in BCN Barclays.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BCN sells stake in BCN Barclays.

text.p: Brazilian private bank BCN has sold its stake in BCN Barclays to Argentine bank Banco de Galicia, an official at BCN Barclays said.

BCN has sold 31.39 percent of BCN Barclays' voting capital and 23 percent of the bank's total capital for roughly 28 million reais, said Ademar Lins de Albuquerque, BCN Barclays president and Barclays PLC country manager.
BCN and BCN Barclays were both moving to the same direction, which encouraged the share sale to avoid competition between the two institutions.
"Our activities were too similar to those of BCN," he said.
With the association with Galicia, BCN Barclays seeks to strengthen its position in Brazil and the Mercosur region, said Albuquerque.

The deal, which still has to be approved by Brazil's and Argentina's central banks, will put an end to a 23-year partnership between BCN and Barclays. BCN Barclays has a net worth of $130 million and assets of $2 billion. The bank is very active in trade finance, Treasury and commercial banking. Albuquerque said the bank plans to eventually enter the asset management business.
